glosses: To work or act together, especially for a common purpose or benefit.

examples.text: In polling by the Pew Research Center in November 2008, fully half the respondents thought the two parties would cooperate more in the coming year, versus only 36 percent who thought the climate would grow more adversarial.

glosses: To allow for mutual unobstructed action.
To function in harmony, side by side.
To obtain the cooperation of (a potential witness); to turn (someone) into a cooperating witness.

examples.text: The best progress is made by combining the practice of coöperation with the science of coöperation. They are one and inseparable to the fullest benefit. But the real way to coöperate is to coöperate.

Higher up the river General Nodzu's army was attaching the Chinese walled town of Ping-yang.
